_provenance: Kepler's third law as an EMERGENT fact, not an assumed one. The genome sets initial positions/velocities; the objective verifies that the grown system OBEYS orbital mechanics. Design Law 1: the simplest rules produce the richest order.

walls.kepler_r2_worst: Period MUST scale as radius^1.5 across the WORST restart. R^2 below 0.90 means the system does not orbit — it tumbles. Kepler's law is the only terminal: it comes from Newton, not taste.
walls.kepler_slope_mean: The fitted Kepler exponent MUST land in [1.3, 1.7]. Below 1.3 means inner planets are too slow (binding too weak); above 1.7 means outer ones are too fast (the central mass does not dominate). Both are broken solar systems.
walls.n_planets_worst: Every restart MUST produce at least 3 bound, orbiting planets. One survivor is an asteroid belt, not a system — the domain's name is bigbang, not scatter.
walls.central_frac_mean: At least 90% of total mass MUST collapse to the central body. A system where most mass escapes or stays diffuse never formed a star, and planets without a dominant central mass have no stable orbits.
walls.merges_late_worst: Late mergers MUST be rare. A system still colliding at t=end has not thermalized — its orbital elements are transient, not stable. Each late merge re-randomizes the Kepler fit.
walls.lz_drift_worst: Angular momentum MUST be conserved. Drift above 5% means the integrator is leaking — the physics reporting its own Kepler slope is not the physics that actually ran.
